clue.text: Last month, gold made up the colour scheme

parts.note: December, the last month of the year, abbreviates to Dec
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Last month someone painted a room's colour scheme in gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made up' is a link meaning 'formed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Décor is the furnishing and colouring style of a room, its overall scheme.

clue.text: I'd put up with golfers' attitudes and degrees of remoteness

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means the letters are read upwards, so back to front

parts.note: I'd is written ID without the apostrophe
a golfer's stance is the way they stand to address the ball

explanation.surface: Someone tolerates golfers' poses, which are a world away from their own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns ID into DI; 'put up with' looks like 'tolerate' but 'with' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Distances are measures of how far apart things are, how remote they are.

clue.text: Top gear for fellow over the water?

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over, above, the second one

parts.note: a chap is a fellow, a man
eau is French for water

explanation.surface: A man going abroad across the sea needs some clothing for the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over the water' hints at going abroad, fitting the French EAU.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapeau is a hat, gear worn on the head at the very top.

clue.text: Lots of paper for English farm-butter on the outside

indicators.note: the butting animal sits around the letter for English, enclosing it

parts.note: a ram is a farm animal that butts, so a butter on the farm

explanation.surface: A dairy wraps its farm butter in lots of paper for the English market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butter' is one who butts, not the spread; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A ream is a quantity of paper, traditionally 480 or 500 sheets, and 'reams' means lots.

clue.text: I speed tick that is tailless, to destruction!

definitions.text: I speed tick that is tailless, to destruction!

indicators.note: the letters are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order, as if destroyed
tailless says the word tick loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A gardener races to kill off a parasite, by now down to its last stump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailless' takes K from TICK, leaving TIC; with I SPEED that is shuffled to the answer, and a chemical that speeds ticks to their end is what the whole clue describes. 'that is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemical killer of insects and mites sends ticks speeding to their destruction.

clue.text: In which contestants must not use corners?

definitions.text: In which contestants must not use corners?

parts.words: In which contestants must not use corners?
parts.note: a boxing ring has corners, but a fair, direct contest between just two candidates allows no cornering or evasive tactics

explanation.surface: A rule for a boxing match where nobody may retreat to the corners.
explanation.walkthrough: The picture is boxing, but the phrase is chiefly an election term for a contest with only two candidates.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a contest is direct, two rivals head to head with no angles or sidelines.

clue.text: Othello's ancient!

parts.note: in Shakespeare's play, 'ancient' is an old word for an ensign, the rank held by Othello's treacherous standard-bearer

explanation.surface: A reference to the old man of the Moor of Venice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ancient' looks like 'old person' but is the Elizabethan word for ensign, the villain's military rank in the play.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare names the Moor's scheming ensign, called his ancient, in the play.

clue.text: Decimally, point is powerful

parts.note: counting decimally is counting in tens
E (east) is a compass point

explanation.surface: Decimal points make the figures powerful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense means strong or extreme, having great force.

clue.text: Muse bringing out tear over love

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over, above, the second
bringing out suggests the letters are worked into a new arrangement

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A poet's inspiration brings tears over a love affair.
explanation.walkthrough: TEAR shuffled gives ERAT, placed over O.
explanation.definitionFit: The nine Muses of Greek myth include the one who presided over love poetry.

clue.text: To open main south-east with a town division

parts.note: a ward is an electoral division of a town

explanation.surface: A coastal town's south-east ward opens on to the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'main' is the old word for the open sea; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Heading towards the sea means going toward the open ocean, the main.

clue.text: Stand it no more, perhaps? Protest!

indicators.note: perhaps says the letters may be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A protester's cry that they can stand it no more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' shuffles STAND IT NO MORE into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A demonstration is a public march or rally of protest.

clue.text: Great at organising boatraces…

indicators.note: organising means putting the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is good at arranging rowing events.
explanation.definitionFit: A regatta is a meeting of rowing or sailing races.

clue.text: … those which do not begin to make champions!

indicators.note: the word loses its first letter, so it does not begin

parts.note: those points back to the boatraces of the previous clue, so the word is races

explanation.surface: Races with no proper start produce winners all the same.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this clue to the one before: 'those' are the races. 'which' and 'to make' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Aces are experts or star performers, the best in their field.

clue.text: Circuit of a doctor, it follows

indicators.note: follows places the word it after the other pieces

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A doctor makes rounds, and a sequence of visits follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambit is a scope or extent, the boundary or compass around something.

clue.text: Ruin a French party

parts.note: un is French for a
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A French party gets ruined.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo someone is to bring about their downfall.

clue.text: Pitch in street and hit the road

indicators.note: in puts the pitch inside the street abbreviation

parts.note: pitch is the black sticky substance tar

explanation.surface: Workers pitch tar into the street and hit the road surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hit the road' looks like a resurfacing job, but it is slang for setting off.
explanation.definitionFit: To set off on a journey is to begin, to get going.

clue.text: Not the only bird left on the river

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the letter sits below the river

parts.note: the Ouse is a river in England, one of several of that name

explanation.surface: A lone bird was left on the river, but it has company.
explanation.walkthrough: The name covers more than one bird: the blackbird, the ring ousel and the water ousel or dipper, hence 'Not the only'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ousel is the old name for the blackbird, and is shared with the ring ousel and the dipper.

clue.text: Room for F A's to be making census of M Ps?

definitions.text: Room for F A's to be making census of M Ps?

parts.words: Room for F A's to be making census of M Ps?
parts.note: an office for financial accountants, read as tallying up the members of the House of Commons

explanation.surface: Accountants need an office where they can count members of parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: The House is the House of Commons, whose MPs are counted at a division.
explanation.definitionFit: This was an old office where a merchant's accounts and money were kept and reckoned.

clue.text: Counsel putting obstruction around street

indicators.note: around puts the obstruction about the street abbreviation

parts.note: a barrier is an obstruction

explanation.surface: A lawyer obstructs the road by putting up a roadblock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a barrister is a lawyer who pleads in the higher courts, a counsel.

clue.text: How Adam presented himself in court?

definitions.text: How Adam presented himself in court?

parts.words: How Adam presented himself in court?
parts.note: the Bible's earliest man committed the earliest sin, so he came to judgment as a newcomer to wrongdoing in the very beginning

explanation.surface: A question about Adam's appearance before a judge.
explanation.walkthrough: Adam was both the earliest man and the earliest sinner, so before God he was literally the first to offend.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone convicted of a crime for the very first time is a newcomer to crime.

clue.text: Producer of first-day covers?

parts.note: in Genesis, Adam and Eve covered themselves with leaves from a tree in Eden; first-day covers are also stamped envelopes

explanation.surface: A stamp collector asks who issues commemorative envelopes.
explanation.walkthrough: First-day covers are envelopes postmarked on a stamp's issue day; here the covers are Adam and Eve's leaves in the first days.
explanation.definitionFit: The fig plant supplied the leaves Adam and Eve sewed into aprons in Eden.

clue.text: Fabric disposed of per yard?

indicators.note: disposed means arranged, so the letters are set out anew

explanation.surface: Cloth is sold off at so much per yard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposed of' looks like 'got rid of', but 'disposed' means arranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Drapery is cloth or textile goods, especially hung in folds.

clue.text: Golden retriever's vessel

parts.note: Jason, who retrieved the Golden Fleece, sailed in a famous ship of Greek myth

explanation.surface: A dog's drinking bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: A golden retriever is a dog, but here it is Jason retrieving the Golden Fleece.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the ship of Jason and his Argonauts on their quest.

clue.text: Lofty sort of wit

explanation.surface: A high-minded kind of humour.
explanation.definitionFit: A loft is the roof space of a house; Athenian (from Attica) refined humour is called Attic wit.

clue.text: Tyne coal, for example, makes vehicle run

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
to go is to run, as of a machine

explanation.surface: Coal from the Tyne keeps a vehicle running.
explanation.walkthrough: Tyne coal, shipped from Newcastle, is the classic example of goods carried by ship; 'makes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Coal shipped from the Tyne is freight, goods carried by ship.

clue.text: Laid off Salvador

indicators.note: off suggests the letters are out of order

explanation.surface: Someone named Salvador was made redundant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laid off' reads as sacked, but 'off' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvador is the first name of the surrealist painter from Spain.

clue.text: Last stand for German drink

explanation.surface: A final stand for German beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A coffin rests on a stand before burial, its final support; Bier is German for beer.

clue.text: Dry part of Kalahari Desert

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A dry stretch of the Kalahari Desert.
explanation.definitionFit: Parched land with little rain is waterless, like a desert.

clue.text: Determining centre of goals aimed at

indicators.note: the centre of the word is its middle letters, with the ends cut away

explanation.surface: Deciding the middle of the targets to aim for.
explanation.definitionFit: Termini are end points or terminal goals, destinations.

clue.text: It can be torture for chaps in the wrong

indicators.note: in places the chaps within the legal wrong

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
chaps are men

explanation.surface: Men in the wrong may suffer torture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It can be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Torment is extreme suffering, physical or mental agony.

clue.text: Kind of sale sought by potter?

explanation.surface: A pottery firm wants a sale to clear its stock.
explanation.walkthrough: The potter is a snooker player potting balls, who hopes to clear the table.
explanation.definitionFit: A sale to clear old stock; and in snooker, potting every remaining ball in one visit.

clue.text: Wash-house aid from Derry?

indicators.note: from here says the letters are made from those of the town name, rearranged

explanation.surface: Laundry equipment shipped from Derry in Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: Derry is a city in Northern Ireland, and the question mark flags that its name is shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: A tumble machine that removes moisture is laundry equipment.
